statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement, so there is no current price path to score. Friday's inside-range close, a rotational two-way session and a VIX near the low end of its 52-week range keep Tail in the low band.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. One window is flagged: the CME Globex reopen from 22:00Z on 27 September, where an unpriced weekend set — a rejected Hormuz reopening plan and intercepted Houthi launches at Saudi targets — meets a 10-year yield at 5.18% and the thinnest liquidity of the week.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 6; unpriced Gulf escalation and a 5.18% 10-year frame the 22:00Z reopen
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures have not traded since Friday 25 September settled at 21:00Z, so this assessment contains no live price-path evidence and says so explicitly. The newest verified tape remains Friday's session: front NQ futures settled at 30,889.25, up 0.40%, inside a 30,679.00-30,997.25 range, while the cash Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 daily range and about 0.53% below the 30,770.63 52-week high. The VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 against a 13.38-35.30 52-week range. The S&P 500 closed at 7,743.41 (+0.51%), the Nasdaq Composite at 27,068.72 (+0.48%) and the Dow at 51,828.62 (+0.93%, or 478.64 points), which delivered weekly gains for all three major indexes.

Friday's internals remain the clearest evidence against a pathological path. Delayed latest-session context shows Technology +0.85% against Communication Services -0.58%, with Semiconductor Equipment & Materials +1.76%, Semiconductors +0.56% and Software - Infrastructure +1.19% against Software - Application -0.50%. Megacap dispersion was wide in the same delayed set, with Microsoft +3.66% against Meta -3.33%, and within semis Qualcomm +3.97% against Intel -3.45%. A rotational session in which leadership changed hands while the index still closed higher is mean reversion working, not failing. That context is labelled non-real-time, its source as-of is not provided, the shared collector payload read this run is roughly 3.6 hours old with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, and none of it can establish current NQ structure.

The macro backdrop is where Stress lives. The 10-year Treasury yield stands at 5.18%, described in Friday reporting as the highest since the financial crisis, with the 2-year at 4.87% and the 30-year at 5.47% in the latest H.15 release for 24 September; the 30-year level is characterised as its highest in more than 20 years. The Federal Reserve raised rates a quarter point in mid-September and signalled another increase before year-end, with market pricing above 60% for a further hike at the October meeting. Equities absorbed that bond move because oil eased: WTI fell 2.33% to $92.41 and is about 7.4% lower on the week, with Brent at $104.32, still roughly 20% higher on the month and 51% higher on the year. Core PCE ran 3.3% year on year through July and is next updated on 30 September, with the September payrolls report on 2 October; Reuters reporting puts consensus near 100,000 jobs and a 4.2% unemployment rate.

Two weekend developments arrived while the market was shut and therefore remain unpriced. On 26 September Washington rejected Tehran's seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Over the same weekend Saudi air defences were reported to have intercepted two Houthi drones aimed at the Riyadh area and one ballistic missile aimed at Khamis Mushait, while Hormuz transit traffic remained around 75% below pre-conflict levels and the US average gasoline price reached $4.49 a gallon against $4.10 a month earlier. Both developments sit inside a long-running campaign that equity markets have repeatedly discounted, and the launches were intercepted rather than landing, so they raise Stress and cap Confidence rather than Tail. The single flagged window is the CME Globex reopen from 22:00Z on 27 September, where that unpriced news set meets the thinnest liquidity of the week. Tail would only leave the low band on observed evidence after the reopen: shallow or absent pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, or price holding near a session extreme.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 05:00Z on Saturday 26 September to 04:00Z on Sunday 27 September, entirely inside the weekend halt that began at Friday's 21:00Z settlement. Every hour carries a published Claude assessment. Tail eased from 8 to 6 as Friday's inside-range close and declining implied volatility aged without contradiction, Stress rose from 46 to 56 on the rate and Gulf backdrop, and Confidence drifted from 84 down to 70 as price evidence aged. No hour in the window recorded persistent one-way structure or a failed retracement sequence.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are almost entirely a closed market: CME Globex equity-index futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday 27 September, the eighteenth slot of this forecast. Conditional Tail therefore eases to 5 through the dead hours, ramps back toward 11 as the reopen approaches, and peaks at 18 in the reopen hour before easing to 15, 13, 11, 10 and 9 as live discovery resumes. Stress runs between 54 and 61 on a 10-year at its highest since the financial crisis, a 30-year at a 20-year high, better-than-60% odds of an October Fed hike, a rejected seven-day Hormuz reopening plan, intercepted weekend Houthi launches at Saudi targets, and crude about 7.4% lower on the week. Confidence decays to 62 in the last closed hours before recovering to 77 once roughly six hours of live tape exist. Every slot maps to EA_ON, and the only flagged window is 22:00Z to 23:59Z.
